transcript:
Meeting header: NorthArc Systems - GPU Channel Orchestration Intro
Date/Time: 2027-04-06 16:00 PT | Duration: ~48m
Attendees: Jules (Redwood AE), Ravi (Redwood SE), Maya (Redwood CSM), Lena (NorthArc VP Product), Markus (NorthArc CTO), Priya (NorthArc Infra), Duncan (NorthArc SA)

Auto Summary (auto-gen - may be imperfect): partner intro + technical discovery. NorthArc evaluating a channel reseller/integrator model, wants predictable throughput for inference workloads, some regulated data, interest in private deployment + hosted fallback.

[00:00] Jules (AE): Hey everyone thanks for joining. we're super excited to talk through how Redwood could plug into NorthArc's channel and GPU orchestration plans. quick intros?
[00:15] Lena: Hi yep I'm Lena, VP product, lead on the AI platform. Markus is CTO, Priya is infra, duncan handles solutions.
[00:28] Markus: morning — we sketched a few architectures, want to see fit and cost.
[00:35] Jules: Great. Ravi, do you want to kick to technical?
[00:40] Ravi (SE): Sure. quick note, i'll try to keep it high level then dig where you want. we're Redwood Inference — we offer hosted API, dedicated pools, and a private deployment option for customers who need VPC or onprem with KMS. sometimes the speech-to-text on our notes flips KMS to "KMSK" so apologies.
[01:05] Priya: on-prem is important. we have customer data that needs to stay behind our firewall for a subset of tenants.
[01:12] Ravi: totally. so two main patterns we see: 1) run Redwood Private in your cloud/VPC or on-prem and expose a local endpoint, or 2) use Redwood Dedicated (reserved GPU pools) with VPC peering + private peering to keep traffic internal. both support RBAC/SSO and can integrate with your KMS for key ownership.
[01:30] Lena: cost is huge for us. we do a lot of low-latency customer serving — latency and cost tradeoffs.
[01:38] Jules: Understood. we typically recommend a hybrid: sensitive inference runs on Private pinned models (quantized), high-throughput non-sensitive on Dedicated or hosted fallback. that lets you manage unit-cost and SLOs.
[02:05] Duncan: quick question — hardware? we currently standardize on A100s in our DCs, but evaluating H100 in cloud. curious about Redwood's support for mixed GPU fleets and routing.
[02:18] Ravi: we support both; the runtime will route by policy — you can route by latency, cost, or region. if capacity is tight on H100, we can fall back to a quantized A100 variant. note: our fallback logic sometimes gets transcribed as "fall-back to a quants variant" in the auto notes.
[02:40] Markus: cool. curious about KV cache and batching — our workloads have variable sequence lengths. how do you keep latency predictable with batching?
[02:52] Ravi: continuous batching plus prefix/KV caching. we tune batch windows per route; for short requests we keep micro-batching small. also you can configure policy for strict latency SLO which prioritizes throughput vs cost tradeoff. worth calling out compilation/kernels — for H100 we switch to optimized 8-bit kernels and shard cache differently.
[03:18] Priya: security — SOC2 is baseline, but we also need audit logs, tenant-level encryption, and HSM/KMS. what do you provide?
[03:28] Jules: we have SOC 2 Type II, can provide encryption at rest with customer-managed KMS and optional HSM integration for Private. audit logs and request-level tracing are available via the Redwood Console; we can push logs to your SIEM over a secure forwarder.
[03:45] Lena: what about data retention? some partners want 30 day retention, others require zero retention by default.
[03:52] Ravi: retention is policy configurable per route — zero retention for regulated tenants is supported in Private and Dedicated. Hosted by default retains metadata for 30 days unless configured otherwise.
[04:10] Markus: let's talk integration model. NorthArc is thinking a channel model where we resell Dedicated capacity to our clients, or we could host Private deployments for end-customers and manage the L2 support. how do we license and bill?
[04:25] Jules: two options — reseller (we provide partner pricing/commissions) or MSP/managed option where you run Redwood Private and we license the software. billing integration can be via consolidated invoices or API-level metering for internal chargeback. i will share the partner deck with the draft MOU.
[04:45] Duncan: what's the onboarding burden? time to a pilot?
[04:49] Ravi: typical pilot (benchmarks + small customer) 3-6 weeks. if you already have infra diagrams and datasets, we can accelerate.
[04:58] Priya: we want a proof of performance on our real workload — not synthetic. will need an NDA and a test plan.
[05:05] Jules: makes sense. we'll prepare a benchmark plan, dataset handoff instructions, and a security pack (NDA + SOC2 + architecture).
[05:15] Lena: any competitor gotchas we should watch? we've looked at ApexFusion and NebulaCloud — both have reseller programs but vary on private deployment automation.
[05:26] Ravi: right — ApexFusion is wallet friendly but their private offering is more manual; NebulaCloud has strong infra but less fine-grained batching controls. Redwood's position is production-first sampling: predictable unit economics and rollout controls.
[05:44] Markus: ok, technical — how would the peering look? will you need a VPN, or AWS Transit?
[05:51] Ravi: we support peering via Transit Gateway, VPC peering, or site-to-site VPN for on-prem. Private control plane deploys in your VPC and the data path never leaves your network for Private mode. for Dedicated we do private peering and encrypted channels.
[06:10] Priya: and KMS ownership — can keys stay in our account?
[06:14] Jules: yes, customer-managed KMS keys are supported, and for high-compliance customers we can integrate with your HSM. sometimes this is noted in our notes as "HSM wonk" — ignore that.
[06:28] [07:00] (jump forward)
[07:05] Ravi: wanted to show a quick rough architecture sketch i pasted into the chat — link: https://redwood.ai/partner-deck/northarc (note: placeholder).
[07:14] Lena: got it. looks like we'd run a Private control plane in our AWS accounts and use Dedicated pools for overflow?
[07:20] Ravi: exactly. Private for sensitive tenants, Dedicated or Hosted for public workloads. routing policy ties them.
[07:32] Markus: fallback timing — if Dedicated saturates, how quickly can requests move to hosted without breaking auth?
[07:38] Ravi: the routing policy supports graceful fallback — tokens and identity are federated via SAML/OIDC; we exchange short-lived credentials so the transition is seamless. coupling with cache warmup is the main chop — warmup takes a few seconds for large KV caches.
[08:00] Priya: how do you handle model versioning and rollouts — we need canary and A/B test capability for safety.
[08:09] Ravi: Redwood Console supports canary rollouts, percent traffic split, and auto-fallback. you can bind prompt/eval suites to watch quality regressions. we also support function/tool calling but sometimes the transcript turns that into "funk and tool calling" which is cute.
[08:35] Lena: performance numbers? tokens per second?
[08:39] Ravi: depends on model and batch size — rough: H100 fp16 can do X tokens/s for long-form, but a better deliverable is a benchmark plan with your payloads. we'll propose both latency targets and cost per 1k tokens using our Optimize recommendations.
[09:00] Duncan: do you run quantized models for cost saving?
[09:05] Ravi: yes, int8 and 4-bit quant profiles where quality is acceptable; we produce QC reports so you can decide. recommended pattern: quantize for bulk non-sensitive outputs, full precision for high-fidelity outputs.
[09:30] Markus: on the pilot, we'd want to test: 1) end-to-end latency from user edge to inference, 2) failover from Private to Dedicated, 3) billing and metering integrity. can Redwood provide instrumentation traces we can ingest?
[09:47] Jules: yes — we'll send trace hooks and you can ingest into your existing tracing/observability. also we'll provide token-level cost breakdowns in the Console.
[10:05] Lena: what's the expected cost delta between Dedicated and hosted for our workloads?
[10:10] Ravi: variable; Dedicated gives lower per-token cost when you commit, Hosted is higher but zero ops. we'll run numbers in the benchmark.
[10:20] Priya: uptime SLA for Dedicated?
[10:23] Jules: Dedicated has SLA-backed uptime and latency targets depending on contract tier; Private depends on your infra. for channel reselling there's an enterprise package with higher SLAs.
[10:35] Markus: curious about multi-tenancy in Private — will we need to isolate for certain customers?
[10:40] Ravi: you can do tenant isolation at the network and runtime level; options for per-customer model pinning and restricted KV caches.
[11:00] [11:20] Lena: commercial model question — if NorthArc resells, how does Redwood handle support? will our team be first line?
[11:27] Maya (CSM): typically partner models vary — resellers can be first line with Redwood second line; or we do joint-support. we have a partner enablement pack and run technical onboarding workshops.
[11:40] Duncan: integration points — auth, billing, and marketplace provisioning. do you have an API for provisioning Dedicated pools?
[11:47] Ravi: yes — provisioning APIs + console flows. also marketplace listings for quick capacity purchases.
[12:05] Markus: are there reference architectures for hybrid customers?
[12:09] Jules: yes. we'll include 2-3 reference docs in the pack: MSP-managed Private, reseller Dedicated, and pure Hosted fallback.
[12:23] Markus: any gotchas on data egress costs when moving from Private to Hosted?
[12:28] Ravi: yes, network egress can be material; our recommendation is to keep sensitive data in-cloud and use hosted fallback only for non-sensitive payloads or to pre-warm caches. we'll include egress cost modeling in the benchmark.
[12:45] [13:30] (customer asks for timeline and pilot framing)
[13:33] Jules: pilot framing idea: 4-week technical benchmark (week 1: infra setup & NDA; week 2: dataset handoff + dry runs; week 3: perf runs + canary; week 4: results, cost model, and pilot sign-off).
[13:52] Priya: fine. need to schedule an NDA before dataset handoff.
[13:57] Jules: we'll send NDA and partner MOU.
[14:05] Lena: on metrics we care about: p95 latency, cost per 1k tokens, failure rate, and warmup time.
[14:13] Ravi: noted — we'll include those in the benchmark plan.
[14:20] Markus: operations - do you support autoscaling policies and burst capacity?
[14:24] Ravi: yes — autoscaling policies, burst capacity windows, and pre-warm policies for scheduled traffic.
[14:35] Duncan: monitoring retention and logs — can we push logs to our SIEM?
[14:40] Maya: yes. we'll set up a secure log forwarder; we can retain logs as you choose per route.
[15:00] [15:30] (closing and commercial touch)
[15:33] Lena: what's the immediate ask for us?
[15:36] Jules: send us infra diagrams, NDA signed, and a small sample dataset. we'll deliver the benchmark plan and partner deck.
[15:45] Markus: timeline — aim to start pilot mid-April?
[15:48] Jules: that's doable; we'll aim to have docs shipped by Friday (2027-04-09) and benchmark kickoff the following week.
[16:00] Priya: one more — our legal needs to see data handling clause for reseller model.
[16:05] Jules: will include in the MOU.
[16:12] (wrap)
[16:15] Jules: thanks everyone. Maya will coordinate follow-up. we'll send the deck, NDA link, and benchmark draft.
[16:25] Lena: thanks, bye.
[16:28] Markus: thanks.
[16:32] (call ends)

Notes/Artifacts referenced: https://redwood.ai/partner-deck/northarc (placeholder), benchmark-proposal-template.xlsx (will be shared), partner-mou-draft.pdf (will be shared).
